research: Line: 76ers -12.5, total 234.5. Covers' Oct 24 2026 preview listed Bucks +12.5 / 76ers -12.5 at about 50/51%. Dimers' Oct 24 write-up cited Bucks +11.5 (-109, BetRivers) and +12.5 elsewhere. The slate's +12.5 is at or slightly better than the market for Milwaukee, so there's no clear line value (spread-specific).

[angle] Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to Miami. Milwaukee's leading scorers are now newcomers Tyler Herro, Kasparas Jakucionis and Jaime Jaquez Jr. (Covers, Oct 24 2026). This is a brand-new roster with only two games of data.
Milwaukee is 2-0 and is scoring 113.1 points per 100 possessions (13th), with 17.0 threes made a game (2nd) on 43.5 attempts (3rd) (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps Milwaukee: the underdog can score.
Milwaukee is on the second night of a back-to-back after allowing 135 points to Chicago on Friday (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps Philadelphia.

Philadelphia is 2-0 and 4th in points allowed per 100 (97.1), but 23rd on offense (103.8 per 100) and 21st in threes made (9.0) (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Mixed: their defense helps Philly, and the weak offense limits its margin, which helps Milwaukee.

[angle] Philadelphia's top end is stacked: Jaylen Brown (25.3 projected points), Tyrese Maxey (24.3), Joel Embiid (22.9) and LeBron James (18.3) are four of the game's top five projected scorers (Dimers, Oct 24 2026). Helps Philadelphia, but the market has clearly priced it at -12.5.

Dimers' model projected 76ers 122-111 (an 11-point margin), with Bucks +12.5 covering 54.5% and named that its top value bet (Dimers, Oct 24 2026). Leans Milwaukee by about 1.5 points (spread-specific). Per LESSONS, a model disagreement this small is not an edge.

Covers' top pick was Bucks +12.5, playable down to +10, on Milwaukee's roughly 10-point-per-100 offensive edge over Philadelphia. The writer noted Philly's 23-26 ATS mark when opponents make a lot of threes (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps Milwaukee; ATS splits are priced.

Over is 6-0 in Milwaukee's last six games as a road underdog, and Milwaukee was 9-6 ATS on no rest in 2025-26 (Covers, Oct 24 2026). That record was built with Giannis, so it has low relevance. Slightly helps Milwaukee.
Philadelphia allows 49.5 rebounds a game and ranks 28th in opponents' defensive rebounding (Covers, Oct 24 2026). A small edge for Milwaukee on second chances.
Moneyline about 16% Bucks / 82-84% 76ers (Covers, Dimers, Oct 24 2026). Consistent with a 12-12.5 point spread.
No injury report was found for either team. The previews list none, which leaves Embiid's and Brown's minutes uncertain this early in the season.
games.reasoning: Every source has the market at 11.5-12.5, the same as the slate, so the number offers no value. Milwaukee's hot three-point shooting on a new roster is offset by the back-to-back and Philadelphia's top-four defense. My projection of Philly by about 11.5 is 1 point off the spread, well inside the pass zone. The [angle] that Giannis is gone and the Bucks still started 2-0 on threes is real, but two games is too small a sample to call it unpriced. A sign of rest for Embiid or Brown, or the market at 13.5+, would have changed it.

research: Line movement: Spurs were -10.5 on Friday evening and moved to -12.5 after the Cooper Flagg news (Predictem, Oct 24 2026). Dimers' Oct 24 2026 page later listed Spurs -14.5 / Mavs +14.5 (Polymarket, 52/50¢). That is about 4 points of movement toward San Antonio, and the slate's -12.5 is 2 points better than the later market (spread-specific, helps San Antonio).
Cooper Flagg is out with left shoulder soreness after a foul in Indianapolis (Predictem and Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio.

Kyrie Irving, 19 months after a torn ACL, was uncertain or on a minutes restriction and expected to have a limited workload on the second night of a back-to-back (Predictem and Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio.

Dallas is also without Dereck Lively II, Santi Aldama, Caleb Martin, Jett Howard and Tarik Biberovic, and Daniel Gafford is limited to 20-22 minutes (Predictem citing Dallas Sports Journal; Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio: Dallas has very thin frontcourt depth against Wembanyama.

[angle] Dallas scored 77 in the first half at Indiana with Flagg and only 44 in the second half without him, losing the half 62-44 after leading 75-40 (Covers and Predictem, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio, since the Mavs' offense collapses without Flagg.

[angle] Both teams are on a back-to-back. San Antonio made a short trip from Austin after Friday's 114-110 loss to Houston; Dallas flew home from Indiana after a Friday night game (Predictem, Oct 24 2026). The rest is equal but Dallas has the harder travel, which slightly helps San Antonio.
[angle] The Spurs are 0-2 after losing to Oklahoma City (Wembanyama 1-of-13) and Houston, and are hunting their first win (Predictem and Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio's motivation.

Last season the Spurs covered all four meetings with Dallas, won them by an average of 19.3 points, and averaged 134.3 points against Dallas, their most against any opponent (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps San Antonio, but head-to-head history is a tiebreaker at most.
Naji Marshall averaged 19.1 ppg in 10 games without Flagg last season and has scored 15+ in both games this season (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Helps Dallas a little, since someone can still score.

Dimers' model projected Spurs 120-109 (11 points) and gave Mavericks +14.5 a 52.1% cover chance, valuing Dallas (Dimers, Oct 24 2026). Earlier, at +12.5, Dimers' top value bet was Mavs +12.5 (55.8%). Helps Dallas (spread-specific), but per LESSONS a model disagreeing with the line isn't an edge.

Covers' top pick was Spurs -12.5, tradeable up to 13.5 (Covers, Oct 24 2026). Predictem took the Under 231.5 and projected Spurs 117-105 (12 points), saying -12.5 had 'lost much of its value' after the Flagg news (Predictem, Oct 24 2026). Mixed (spread-specific).
Close to 60% of tickets were on the Over (Predictem, Oct 24 2026). Neutral for the side.
games.reasoning: What decided it was market position. The line went from -10.5 to -12.5 on the Flagg news and later showed -14.5, so the slate's -12.5 sits about 2 points short of where the market moved. That is the one edge LESSONS says has paid, and after a 3+ point move the new number is treated as fair. Taking the fair number as Spurs by 14.5 gives a 2-point edge. That isn't 'strong', and it is laying points with a favorite, which LESSONS says to be careful with, hence only a lean. The most surprising [angle] is the depth of Dallas's injury list: Flagg, Lively, Aldama and Martin are out, and Irving and Gafford are limited. If the -14.5 was only a stray prediction-market quote and the consensus stayed at -12.5, this would be a pass.
